html:
Ban Chiang is a village in northeast Thailand where people lived, farmed rice and buried their dead for over 2,000 years, from about 1500 BCE. It is famous for its painted pottery and early bronze.

The site was found in 1966, when an American student tripped over pots sticking out of a village road. Digs revealed burials with pots, bronze bracelets and later iron tools. The early dates once claimed for its bronze have since been revised later.

The red-painted pots, from its last centuries, became a symbol of Thai prehistory. Ban Chiang became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992. Compare rice at Khok Phanom Di and the Plain of Jars in Laos.
sum: Ban Chiang is a village in northeast Thailand where people lived, farmed rice and buried their dead for over 2,000 years, from about 1500 BCE. It is famous for its painted pottery and early bronze.
